fun_highlights: The callback system (cb_* cards) is the single best mechanic for a completionist. Watching Calla's kept-book resurface 43 years later in Dynasty 4 ('Read, at last with ease, the book that began everything at age 7') or the lookaway-child echo paying off decades on is exactly the long-arc closure this genre promises. These are rare, memory-gated, and feel earned — they reward playing multiple lives.

The era layer adds genuine contextual variety that a completionist will want to exhaust. Dynasty 4 (Elias born into war years) reads materially differently from Dynasty 13 (plenty, then turning). The three-variant era text pools mean the 'sickness in the land' opener lands with different phrasing in Dynasties 6, 7, and 10 — enough to feel like new content even when the underlying beat is the same.

The drifter vocation arc ('y_adrift' branching into a distinct life-shape) is a genuine discovery reward. A completionist chasing rare paths will notice that the adrift track generates cards ('a_adrift', 'm_adrift', 'e_adrift') that never fire in soldier/scholar/maker lives, and the ambivalence prose (Noor's 'ache, quietly, for an anchor' vs 'lean into the range, be unplaceable') creates a real philosophical fork with two satisfying outcomes.

The motto crystallisation system gives the dynasty layer a concrete long-game goal. Completionists will recognise the 9 reputation tracks, hunt the 3-variants-per-track motto pool (27 possible mottoes, de-duplicated across houses per session), and feel real satisfaction when 'We earn the bread we eat' appears after 4 generations of industrious play. Dynasty 4 Okonkwo earning it on Noor's death line is a well-paced payoff.

Early-death lives (Dynasties 7 gen-1 Joaquin at 16, Dynasty 8 Linnea at 18, Dynasty 15 gen-2 Theda at 10) are executed with restraint and distinctly flavoured epitaphs ('Gone too soon, with so much unspent' / 'Left before the story had found its middle') that make short lives feel dramatically complete rather than truncated. A completionist will want to collect these — and they are genuinely short enough to be repeatable.

The bequest card (e_bequest) with four distinct options ('Everything I know', 'Every coin I can spare', 'The stories, and the warmth', 'Nothing but their own freedom') creates a real mechanical lever across the generation boundary with visible downstream effects in the heir's starting stats. This is the best example of the dynasty layer doing something that individual-life games cannot.
staleness: The body-decline observation lines are the loudest repetition problem in the transcripts. Between Dynasties 6 and 15, virtually every life past age 55 triggers at least one of: 'The stairs have started to ask a question of them', 'The body has begun sending its small bills', 'The weather has begun living in his joints', 'The body keeps its own ledger now', or a near-synonym. The vit_tire pool is 18 lines and the vit_neg pool is 16, but the per-life cap of 4 (P._obsN) means a typical long life hits 2-3 of these — and they all express the same thing with slight paraphrase. Across 15 dynasties the reader has seen body-decline prose 25-30 times and all of it sounds the same.

The calling card (y_calling) fires in nearly every life and every transcript shows one of four paths — but the mid-life scholar arc generates a near-identical pair of beats in almost every scholar life: cb_study_pays ('the lean years of study, begun at X, at last came good') followed later by 'give it all away, teach' or 'guard it, dearly bought.' These two beats appear together in Dynasty 2 (Henrik), Dynasty 6 (Tomas), Dynasty 9 (Selma), Dynasty 10 (Tobias as wanderer but structurally similar), Dynasty 11 (Annika). The scholar template feels pre-determined.

The 'meet them halfway / pretend not to notice' love-opening beat fires in 11 of the 15 dynasties, usually framed with the same rotating 7-variant text pool. Because the draw nudge strongly prefers y_love1 in youth (engine.js line 228: chance(0.30) per draw), and because every coupled life then almost always sees a_marry and a_child, the love-marry-child cluster is the MOST REPEATED structural sequence in the transcripts — often all three in the same decade of a life, generating the same domestic framing beats. Dynasties 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 13, 15 all show this cluster.

The ambient 'mind_hi' observation pool leaks 'There is a whole life they keep behind the eyes, and visits often' and near-synonyms into a disproportionate number of lives with high mind scores. Because the scholar vocation gives mind +16 and the bequest system can pass mind bonuses forward, long scholarly dynasties generate this observation in 3-4 consecutive generations. In Dynasty 13 alone, this pool fires for Emory (gen 1), Idris (gen 2 'The mind has become a room he can close the door of'), and Anders gen-5 ('There is a whole life he keeps behind the eyes'). Three different people with the same inner-life observation in the same house.

The war-grief callback ('Lost someone to the war and put the loss away in work, where it kept, badly, for years') fires verbatim in Dynasties 4 (Elias at 38), 4 (Noor at 53), 7 (Caleb at 47), and 14 (Anders at 54). The text is identical each time: 'The war reaches into the house the way it reaches into every house, and takes someone out of it who is not given back.' with the same two-option response. War-era lives frequently generate this beat but there is only one scene text and two choices, making it feel like the same scene on replay.

The 'reckoning with the drifted life' arc produces near-identical late-life prose sequences. In the transcripts, every adrift character who reaches midlife faces the same pair of events in close succession: the 'lean into the range / ache for an anchor' card and the 'grasp late for a single thing / make peace with the drift' card. Calla Okonkwo (Dynasty 4), Noor Okonkwo, Mira Halloran (Dynasty 12), Anders Aldecott (Dynasty 14) all produce this same two-beat sequence in the 45-60 age range. The framing text varies slightly but the choices and outcomes are structurally identical, producing 'the drifter always faces the same existential reckoning at the same age' pattern.

improvements.what: Collapse the body-decline observation pools into a single larger, slower-firing pool with a stricter per-dynasty cooldown on thematic clusters, not just individual lines.
improvements.why: With P._obsN capped at 4 per life and two separate pools (vit_tire, vit_neg), a long dynasty can accumulate 8-10 body-decline observations across 5 generations, all expressing the same 'the body is slowing' note. The real problem is not line-level repetition (the pools are already large) but thematic repetition: every elder phase smells the same. A fix is to cap body-decline at 1 observation per stage (one in midlife, one in elder) per life, and ensure the thematic cluster 'body_decline' is tracked in RECENT_CLUSTERS so it cannot dominate three consecutive generations.

improvements.what: Add 3-4 vocation-specific mid-life divergence cards for the scholar arc that are NOT about whether to teach or guard knowledge — the current arc has cb_study_pays -> knowledge-guard/give as its only branching point after the calling.
improvements.why: The scholar track in content.js has calling -> study_pays -> teach/guard as its structural spine, with almost no other scholar-specific content between ages 28-60. A soldier gets war campaigns (y_calling variant, the war-era cards, the PTSD callback at 3am). A wanderer gets leave/stay, horizon, return-home callbacks. The scholar's unique content thins out past age 30. Adding 2-3 scholar-specific adult moments (a professional dispute, a dangerous idea, a student who surpasses them) would give completionists new content to discover and break the template feel.

improvements.what: Give the war-grief card (the 'takes someone out of it who is not given back' beat) at least 3 distinct scene variants and a third choice option (e.g. 'seek who did this / channel it into action') to break the verbatim repeat.
improvements.why: This is the most visibly copy-pasted scene in the transcripts — same framing, same two choices, same outcome prose, appearing word-for-word in Dynasties 4, 4, 7, and 14. War-era dynasties will reliably generate it in multiple consecutive generations. Even shallow scene-text variation would break the 'I have read this exact paragraph before' recognition.

improvements.what: Add a 'dynasty-unique event' system: 2-3 one-time-per-SESSION cards (not per-life, not per-dynasty) that encode genuinely unusual life-shapes — a character who inherits a family disgrace and must decide whether to expose or perpetuate it, a founding figure who refuses to name an heir at all, a life that ends mid-sentence (the cb_inherited_secret card exists but is rarely triggered). These would give completionists a 'hunting the truly rare' incentive beyond the current motto/heirloom collection.
improvements.why: The completionist lens specifically rewards long-tail discovery. Currently the rarest content is cb_inherited_secret (requires strayed-and-unconfessed passing to a child who discovers it) and the seat-7 pinnacle. Both are achievable but not surprising after several dynasties. A handful of 'have you seen this yet?' beats — with onceDyn:12 or higher — would sustain completionist motivation past dynasty 10.

improvements.what: Introduce inter-generational consequence callbacks that reference the SPECIFIC CHOICES made by named ancestors, not just inherited memory tags. Currently the 'family story' callbacks (the Tomas/Calla/Caleb ancestor-legend cards) fire with generic framing: 'There is a story in the family about [name] — the one remembered for X.' The scene text is the same regardless of what that ancestor actually chose.
improvements.why: Dynasty 7 Caleb ('There is a story about Joaquin — the one taken too soon') and Dynasty 10 Felix ('There is a story about Tobias — who built something') both use the same callback template. The ancestor's actual decisions are not echoed. A completionist who deliberately shaped Tobias's life to be ruthless rather than kind will see the same 'built something' callback as if he had been a teacher. Making these callbacks pull specific decision records from S.lineage (which already stores them) would make dynasties feel causally unique.

verdict: A Life is a solidly crafted meditative life-sim with genuine long-game hooks — the callback system, motto crystallisation, and era variation give a completionist real reasons to keep playing past the third dynasty. The writing quality is consistently above average for the genre and the bequest mechanic is a clever inter-generational lever. The problem, which shows clearly in the 15-dynasty transcript, is that the structural templates are too visible by dynasty 8: the body-decline observation cluster, the love-marry-child sequence, the scholar's teach/guard binary, and the drifter's midlife reckoning all repeat with paraphrase rather than genuine variance. A completionist chasing rare content will hit the bottom of the discovery pool faster than the game's richness suggests they should.
